newsitem.title: USA: Nike sees revenue shortfall up to $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: Nike sees revenue shortfall up to $200 mln.

text.p: Nike Inc chief financial officer Bob Falcone said Thursday the company's revenues for the current fourth quarter will be $150 million to $200 million below analyst expectations.

Falcone said in a conference call with analysts that the revenue shortfall was the main reason the company projects earnings for the quarter of $0.51 to $0.56 per share, compared with a previous consensus estimate of $0.69.
The company also said the earnings will be affected by a onetime charge of $18 million or $0.04 a share to shut down a manufacturing facility at its Bauer Inc. skate division.
Analysts had estimated Nike revenues at about $2.7 billion for the current quarter, which ends Saturday.

Falcone said the revenue shortfall was caused by timing issues in Europe, including a shift by retailers to more advance ordering, and by a shortage of apparel and some order cancellations in the United States.

Falcone said the $30 million in U.S. order cancellations were "not in our estimation a serious problem" compared with overall expected U.S. footwear and apparel revenue of $1.2 billion for the quarter.

"If you look at these items individually none of these really are that significant to the quarter," Falcone said. "But collectively when you add them all up it becomes a significant issue at the top line."
He reiterated that company executives did not expect the problems to spill over into future quarters, and he said Nike expects to regain some of the lost business, particularly in apparel.

"We don't see any significant fundamental change in our business going forward into fiscal year 1998," he said. "We feel very confident our business is as strong as we would expect it to be in the current retail environment."
He said the company still expects revenue from U.S. footwear and apparel sales to grow by 7 to 12 percent in the coming fiscal year, while international business grows about 35 percent.
And he said executives continue to believe total revenues will grow by 15 to 18 percent annually for the next several years.
The conference call was monitored by Reuters on a tape-delayed basis.
